source.version: Published version: The Annals of Statistics 52(2), 842–867 (2024)

enumeration.method: Independent enumeration of actual small-cap THEOREM headings across all 26 published PDF pages, checked against the source images on pages 14,15,17,18. Exactly 3.3,3.5,3.7,5.1,5.2 occur. Restated external results are included; citations and other result labels are excluded. Separate supplement links on page 23 were not opened.

checks: Published title, all authors, volume, issue, page range, DOI, 26-page count and pinned PDF hash checked. Cached page texts match fresh byte-preserving extraction.
Inventory and final census both validate; the independent inventory hash matches and every original claim field survives unchanged.
All five complete theorem statements visually checked on pages 14,15,17,18, including explicit A6, moment orders, approximate-objective references and all asymptotic conditions.
The SDE, filtered experiment, closed parameter domain and true covariance shorthand checked on pages 1 and 6; A1-A5 checked individually on page 7.

The OU integral covariance, affine mean, nonlinear flow, A6 and both exact splitting compositions checked on page 8. The unbarred flow domain and the printed R(h,x_0) covariance remainder are preserved.
Definitions 3.1 and 3.2 checked on page 13, retaining q1>=q2+1/2, conditional errors and all-p moment bounds.
Full objectives and transformed residual checked on page 9; inverse identity and argmin checked on page 10. Their differences from the approximate objectives on page 17 remain explicit.
Half-vectorization order, diagonal alternative, information blocks, true-parameter derivatives and distinct drift/covariance convergence scales checked on pages 17-18.

Independent graph traversal confirms all 39 direct and 50 related connections, with no estimation assumptions imported into generic numerical results and no information matrix imported into consistency.
Every interface has exact source terms, source-kind metadata, meaningful matching highlight selectors and an explanation for every related theorem path.
Eight auxiliary passages and nineteen convention notes preserve essential notation and unresolved source distinctions without changing quoted statements.
The publication ends in references on page 26; supplementary mathematical material and code are separate files and were excluded.

source_notes: The audited source is the published journal article, DOI 10.1214/24-AOS2371, rather than a preprint.
The estimation Theorems explicitly name approximate objectives (22)/(23), while practice uses full objectives (12)/(14). No equivalence of minimizers is assumed.

Inverse existence is stated asymptotically on the open drift domain. Global finite-step invertibility, inverse-growth bounds and behavior at search-boundary parameters are not supplied by that wording.
The inverse-Jacobian identity on page 10 is retained with its original argument, with the argument discrepancy recorded separately.

unresolved_source_references.description: Theorems 5.1 and 5.2 explicitly minimize approximate objectives (22)/(23), while the full estimators in (15) minimize (12)/(14) and the surrounding prose says these full objectives are used in practice. The census does not silently assert identical minimizers or transfer a theorem between them.

The parameter search space in Section 2 is the closure of the product of bounded open convex domains. The true parameter is interior. In contrast, the forward-flow domain, semigroup quantifier and (A6) on page 8 use unbarred Theta_beta. The different printed domains are retained; inverse availability at every boundary search parameter is not asserted.

The initial parameter is (beta,Sigma), the consistency target is (beta,Sigma Sigma^T), and the normality coordinates are (beta,varsigma). The paper explains covariance identifiability but does not explicitly redefine Theta under these coordinate changes. A parameter domain for a future implementation needs to respect this distinction.

The shorthand Sigma Sigma_0^T means the true covariance Sigma_0 Sigma_0^T, not a product of a candidate Sigma with the true transpose. Derivatives of F_0 and the true covariance in (27) are interpreted as differentiating the family before evaluation at the true parameter.

Assumption (A6) says the inverse is defined asymptotically for all x and beta when h tends to zero. It does not specify a uniform small-step threshold over states and parameters, or a global inverse for every finite h. The source itself acknowledges possible nonexistence within the optimization search domain.

Corollary 3.8 proof invokes polynomial growth of the inverse flow. That extra inverse-growth statement is not explicit in (A6). The census preserves (A6) rather than adding this proof claim as a new theorem hypothesis.

The inverse-Jacobian identity printed on page 10 evaluates the forward and inverse Jacobians at the same x. The general inverse-function identity evaluates the forward Jacobian at f_h^{-1}(x). The source formula is archived unchanged and not treated as a verified algebraic identity.

The OU covariance expansion (6) literally ends with the weaker matrix remainder R(h,x_0) after its h and h^2 terms. It is not transcribed as R(h^3,x_0), even though a stronger order is natural from the integral formula.

R is defined for a first argument in (0,1), with polynomial state dependence and an unspecified constant. Theorems use it as order notation, not a fixed common function. The approximate-objective introduction also writes R(Nh^2,x_0), while consistency alone assumes h to zero and Nh to infinity, without Nh^2 to zero.

Strong Lp errors compare paths, so the OU innovations must be coupled to the driving Wiener increments. The source identifies them through the OU flow and states their iid Gaussian law; a distribution-only construction with unrelated independent noise would not preserve the strong comparison.

The grid has N increments and N+1 observations, with T=Nh. Numerical moment/error bounds are on a finite horizon; the estimation Theorems explicitly let the observation horizon diverge. The census does not assume every numerical-bound constant is uniform in a growing horizon.

Definition 3.1 uses a conditional mean error of order q1 and a conditional 2p-moment root of order q2, with q1 at least q2+1/2. Theorem 3.3 uses 2p moments for p>=1; Theorems 3.5 and 3.7 use p moments for p>=2. The printed existential C>=1 is retained even though C does not explicitly occur in the displayed conclusions.

Assumption (A1) explicitly gives C2 regularity for N, while Section 2 only describes A and b as parameterized functions and F as locally Lipschitz. The information matrix needs parameter derivatives of F. The source extraction does not silently add a separate smoothness assumption on A and b.

Assumption (A3) states existence of an invariant probability. It does not itself explicitly assert uniqueness, ergodicity, stationary initialization, or all invariant moments. Assumption (A5) states equality of drifts for every state, not merely almost everywhere under that probability.

Section 2 assumes positive-definite covariance and the estimation Theorems explicitly include (A4). Prose discusses the potential applicability of S to hypoelliptic models, with proofs deferred to a separate paper. Those extensions are not added to the scope of the printed Theorems.

The source vech ordering is S_11,S_12,S_22,...,S_1d,...,S_dd. It must not be replaced by a different triangular ordering without coordinating derivatives and information blocks. For a diagonal covariance the source uses diag instead; its dimension is d rather than the general s=d(d+1)/2.

The source Jacobian convention puts derivative index first. Transposition does not alter the trace used in (23), but the convention should not be silently replaced when interpreting other matrix products. The census records the original definition separately.

The statement minimizers are not accompanied by explicit existence, measurable-selection, tie-breaking or failed-inverse-domain conventions. These are unresolved implementation choices, not extra conditions inserted into the original Theorems.

Theorems 3.3 and 3.5 repeat cited external results but are nevertheless printed as Theorems in the main text and are included. Lemmas, Propositions and Corollaries remain outside the inventory; no supplementary proofs or code have been opened.

ambient_resolution.shared: D1 gives the filtered additive-noise diffusion with deterministic initial state; D2 specifies its linear/nonlinear decomposition, closed parameter search domain, interior true parameter and covariance shorthand. D8 gives N+1 equidistant observations. Euclidean vectors, matrix operations, Gaussian laws, expectations and stochastic convergence are ambient. A1-A3 archive the generic remainder, derivative, closure and additive-constant notation. A4-A8 preserve inverse-flow and full-objective context. Source ambiguities remain explicitly recorded, without certifying proofs.
ambient_resolution.3.3: D1/D3/D4 specify the exact SDE and A1-A2. The numerical process and one-step map are bound in the theorem; D14 is its conditional Lp consistency and D15 its bounded moments. D8 resolves k,N,h; x_0 is the exact initial state. The q1,q2 conditions come from Definition 3.1 and the conclusion uses the generic scalar remainder. No particular splitting, invariant measure or inverse flow is required.
ambient_resolution.3.5: D12 resolves the exact nonlinear-then-OU LT approximation (10), with D9/D10 resolving its stochastic and deterministic steps. D3/D4 are the explicit A1-A2 hypotheses; D1 and D8 resolve the exact solution and grid. The p-moment root, p>=2 and R(h,x_0) conclusion are preserved; no A3-A6 assumptions are imported from the estimation section.
ambient_resolution.3.7: D13 resolves the nonlinear-half/OU-full/nonlinear-half S scheme (11). D3/D4 supply A1-A2 and D11 supplies the explicitly added A6. D1/D8 resolve the exact solution and time grid; D9/D10 recursively resolve the forward steps. The theorem assumes inverse availability although its displayed forward scheme contains no inverse. Invariant probability and identifiability are not additional premises.
ambient_resolution.5.1: D3-D7 and D11 separately unpack A1-A6. D16 is the pair of approximate objectives (22)/(23), with Z from (13) archived as its application context; D9/D10 resolve the OU mean and deterministic flow. D1/D2 give the model, parameter and true covariance. D8 resolves the high-frequency long-horizon limits. The minimizer is bound by the theorem; covariance half-vectorization and the Fisher information are not necessary for this consistency statement.
ambient_resolution.5.2: The same model, A1-A6 and approximate objectives as in Theorem 5.1 are used. D17 resolves varsigma, and D18 resolves the positive-definite matrix C(theta_0) whose inverse is the Gaussian covariance. The two convergence scales are sqrt(Nh) for beta and sqrt(N) for covariance coordinates. The extra Nh^2 tending to zero condition and the explicit interior true-parameter condition are preserved. No particular Lorenz model or comparison estimator is required.

review_limits: Source transcription and statement-prerequisite audit, not proof certification or source repair.
Separate supplementary article and code were excluded.
